newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end higher on economic growth optimism.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end higher on economic growth optimism.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Monday as investors expected healthy economic growth to lead to solid company profits this year, brokers said.
The market would likley rise again Tuesday, they added.
Monday, the General Index rose 1.63 percent to 1,707.18 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 2.19 percent to 2,468.23 points.
In a total of 1,864 trades, volume was a 32.9 million soles ($12.4 million), according to preliminary figures.
The Peruvian economy grew 4.1 percent year-on-year in February compared with 4.2 percent growth in the year to February 1996, the National Institute of Statistics and Information (INEI) said Friday.

The strong growth figure -- published late during Friday's session -- left investors optimistic that the economy would grow in line with the government's target for the year of five percent, brokers said.
Signs of solid growth this year by benchmark Telefonica del Peru were also driving the market up, they added.
"Gross Domestic Product growth turned out to be really good and Telefonica is showing strong potential," Arlen Lahura of local brokerage Interlima said.
Telefonica del Peru closed Monday up 3.88 percent at 6.43 soles in volume of 2.0 million shares. Miner Morococha soared 10.18 percent to 2.49 soles on volume of 375,000 shares.
Polymetal miner Buenaventura climbed 5.65 percent to 24.30 soles on volume of 17,000 shares.
